title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Recognition and Enforcement of Civil Judgments of Courts of the Taiwan Region

articles.content_en: Article 1: The parties to a civil judgment rendered by a court in the Taiwan region, as well as their heirs and assigns, may, pursuant to these Provisions, apply to the People's Court as applicants for recognition and enforcement of the judgment. The opposing party in the judgment shall be the respondent. Where both parties apply for recognition and enforcement, both parties shall be listed as applicants.

Article 2: For the purposes of these Provisions, civil judgments of courts in the Taiwan region include effective civil judgments, rulings, settlement records, mediation records, payment orders, and other instruments rendered by courts in the Taiwan region.
Where an application is made for recognition of an effective judgment, ruling, or settlement record concerning civil damages rendered by a court in the Taiwan region in a criminal case, these Provisions shall apply.
Where an application is made for recognition of a mediation document issued by a township, town, or city mediation committee in the Taiwan region and verified by a court in the Taiwan region, and which has the same effect as an effective civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, these Provisions shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 3: Where an applicant simultaneously applies for recognition and enforcement of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, the People's Court shall first review the application under the recognition procedures and, after ruling to recognize the judgment, the enforcement organ of the People's Court shall enforce it.
Where an applicant applies only for recognition of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, the People's Court shall review whether the judgment should be recognized and render a ruling. If the civil judgment of the court in the Taiwan region contains a payment obligation, the People's Court shall, when accepting the recognition application and rendering the recognition ruling, explain to the applicant that the applicant may apply to the People's Court for enforcement.
Where an applicant directly applies for enforcement, the People's Court shall inform the applicant to submit a recognition application at the same time; if the applicant insists on not applying for recognition, the People's Court shall rule to dismiss the application.

Article 4: Cases involving applications for recognition of civil judgments of courts in the Taiwan region shall be accepted by the Intermediate People's Court or special people's court at the place of domicile or habitual residence of the applicant, or at the place of domicile, habitual residence, or location of property of the respondent.
Where an applicant applies to two or more People's Courts with jurisdiction for recognition, the People's Court that first dockets the case shall have jurisdiction.
Where an applicant applies to the People's Court at the location of the respondent's property for recognition, the applicant shall provide relevant evidence of the existence of the property.

Article 5: Where an applicant entrusts another person to act as agent in applying for recognition of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, the applicant shall submit to the People's Court a power of attorney signed or sealed by the principal.
A power of attorney signed or sealed by a party from the Taiwan region shall undergo relevant notarization or verification procedures, except where the power of attorney has been signed in the presence of a judge of the People's Court through online video or offline witnessing, or where it has been notarized by a notarization organ in Mainland China to prove that it was signed in Mainland China.
Where a party from the Taiwan region who holds a Residence Permit for Taiwan Residents entrusts a lawyer practicing in Mainland China or another person as agent, the power of attorney forwarded to the People's Court by the agent need not be notarized or undergo relevant verification procedures.

Article 8: Where an application meets the conditions prescribed in Articles 4 through 7 of these Provisions, the People's Court shall docket the case within seven days after receiving the application and shall notify the applicant and the respondent. Where an application does not meet the above conditions, the People's Court shall, within seven days, rule not to accept the case and shall state the reasons. If the case has already been accepted, the People's Court shall rule to dismiss the application. If the applicant is dissatisfied with the ruling, it may file an appeal.
Where the materials submitted by the applicant do not meet the requirements, the People's Court shall, in a one-time written notice, inform the applicant to make corrections within a specified period. If corrections are made within the specified period, the period for the People's Court to decide whether to docket the case shall be calculated from the date of receipt of the corrected materials. If no correction is made within the specified period, the application shall be returned and recorded in the files; if the applicant insists on submitting the application, the People's Court shall rule not to accept it. If the application still fails to meet the requirements after correction, the People's Court shall rule not to accept it.
After the People's Court has ruled not to accept the application or to dismiss the application, if the applicant applies again and meets the acceptance conditions, the People's Court shall accept the application.

Article 9: The People's Court shall serve a copy of the written application on the respondent within five days from the date of docketing. The respondent shall submit its opinions within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the copy of the written application; where the respondent has no domicile in Mainland China, it shall submit its opinions within thirty days from the date of receipt of the copy of the written application. If the respondent fails to submit opinions within the above period, it shall not affect the review by the People's Court. Where the respondent applies for an extension, the People's Court shall decide whether to grant it.
Article 10: For a case involving an application for recognition of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, the People's Court shall form a collegiate bench to conduct the review.

Article 11: Where an applicant applies for recognition of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, it shall provide relevant certifying documents to prove that the judgment is authentic and has already become effective. Where the civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region is a default judgment, the applicant shall simultaneously submit certifying documents proving that the court in the Taiwan region had lawfully summoned the party, unless the judgment has clearly stated such fact.
The applicant may apply to the People's Court to ascertain, through the cross-strait judicial assistance channel for investigation and evidence collection, the authenticity and effectiveness of the civil judgment of the court in the Taiwan region and the certifying documents showing that the party was lawfully summoned; where the People's Court deems it necessary, it may also, ex officio, request the Taiwan region through the cross-strait judicial assistance channel to investigate and collect evidence on relevant matters.

Article 12: Where the evidence provided by the applicant, including the civil judgment of the court in the Taiwan region and relevant certifying documents, is transmitted through the cross-strait channel for the use and verification of notarized certificates, the People's Court shall confirm its authenticity, unless there is contrary evidence sufficient to overturn it.

Article 13: Before or after accepting an application for recognition of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, the People's Court may, pursuant to the Civil Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations, rule to adopt preservation measures upon the application of the applicant.

Article 14: After the People's Court has accepted an application for recognition of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, and before rendering a ruling, if the applicant requests withdrawal of the application, the People's Court may rule to permit the withdrawal.

Article 15: After the People's Court accepts an application for recognition of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, it shall conclude the case within six months from the date of docketing. Where there are special circumstances requiring an extension, the People's Court shall report to the next higher people's court for approval.
The period for serving documents and investigating and collecting evidence through the cross-strait judicial assistance channel shall not be counted into the review period.

Article 17: Where, upon review, the People's Court can confirm that the civil judgment of the court in the Taiwan region is authentic and has taken effect, and none of the circumstances listed in Article 16 of these Provisions exists, it shall rule to recognize the effect of the judgment. If it cannot recognize all items of the judgment, it may recognize some of the items. If it cannot confirm the authenticity or effectiveness of the civil judgment, the People's Court shall rule to dismiss the application of the applicant.
For a case where the application is dismissed by ruling, if the applicant applies again and meets the acceptance conditions, the People's Court shall accept the application.

Article 18: A civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region that has been recognized by a ruling of the People's Court shall have the same effect as an effective judgment rendered by the People's Court.

Article 19: A ruling made by the People's Court pursuant to Article 16 or Article 17 of these Provisions shall take legal effect upon service.
If the applicant or the respondent is dissatisfied with the ruling, it may apply to the next higher people's court for reconsideration within ten days from the date of service of the ruling.

Article 20: Where an applicant applies to the People's Court for recognition of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, and the dispute involved in that judgment is the same dispute as the one being tried by the People's Court, the People's Court may rule to suspend the litigation.
Where, after review, the People's Court rules not to recognize the civil judgment of the court in the Taiwan region, the suspended litigation shall be resumed; where it rules to recognize the judgment, the People's Court shall rule to dismiss the prosecution of the suspended litigation.

Article 21: During the period of review of an application for recognition of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, if the applicant or the respondent files a prosecution with the People's Court regarding the same dispute, the People's Court shall rule not to accept it; if it has already been accepted, the People's Court shall rule to suspend the litigation.

Article 22: Where a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region has already been recognized in whole or in part by a ruling of the People's Court, if the applicant or the respondent files a prosecution with the People's Court regarding the part already recognized, the People's Court shall rule not to accept it; if it has already been accepted, the People's Court shall rule to dismiss the prosecution.
Where a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region has been ruled by the People's Court not to be recognized or partially not to be recognized, if the applicant applies again for recognition of the part not recognized, the People's Court shall rule not to accept it; if it has already been accepted, the People's Court shall rule to dismiss the application. However, the applicant may file a prosecution with the People's Court regarding the part not recognized.

Article 23: After a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region is recognized in whole or in part by a ruling of the People's Court, if the applicant applies for enforcement of the recognized part, enforcement shall be carried out pursuant to the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law on enforcement procedures.

Article 24: The period for an applicant to apply for recognition and enforcement of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region shall be governed by Article 250 of the Civil Procedure Law, except that an application for recognition of a judgment of a court in the Taiwan region concerning personal status is not governed by that provision.
Where the applicant applies only for recognition without simultaneously applying for enforcement, the period for applying for enforcement shall be recalculated from the date on which the ruling of the People's Court on the recognition application takes effect.

Article 25: The legal documents made by the People's Court in handling cases involving applications for recognition and enforcement of civil judgments of courts in the Taiwan region shall be served on the applicant and the respondent according to law.

Article 26: For applying for recognition and enforcement of a civil judgment of a court in the Taiwan region, relevant fees shall be paid by reference to the provisions of the Measures for the Payment of Litigation Fees.

Article 27: These Provisions shall come into force on July 1, 2015. The Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Recognition by the People's Courts of Civil Judgments Rendered by Relevant Courts in the Taiwan Region (Fa Shi [1998] No. 11), the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether a People's Court Should Accept an Application for Recognition Filed by a Party Holding a Civil Mediation Document of a Relevant Court in the Taiwan Region or a Mediation Agreement Issued or Confirmed by a Relevant Institution (Fa Shi [1999] No. 10), the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether a People's Court Should Accept an Application for Recognition Filed by a Party Holding a Payment Order of a Relevant Court in the Taiwan Region (Fa Shi [2001] No. 13), and the Supplementary Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Recognition by the People's Courts of Civil Judgments Rendered by Relevant Courts in the Taiwan Region (Fa Shi [2009] No. 4) shall be abolished simultaneously.
